available.origin: Compiled from the supplied TeX without source edits
Generated from the supplied CV records

createDuringImplementation.brief: An original, restrained TQ monogram; never a fabricated portrait.
Small original schematic tree/network identifiers, labelled as illustration where meaning could be confused. No fabricated scientific data.
15 local SVGs matching iconCloudItems; permitted monochrome brands or neutral labelled symbols. Record licence and origin for every file.
An original typography-based social image with name and research title; use the actual framework route convention.
Build-generated derivatives of approved owner photographs. Preserve visual colour and orientation, remove private metadata, reserve dimensions and publish only selected records.

notSupplied.rule: Use the TQ monogram as the deliberate identity design until an authentic portrait is supplied.
Capture the public application only when access and displayed data are appropriate, or request a supplied screenshot. Record capture date, URL and permission context. Do not invent it.
Do not show a video dialog until a real recording exists.
Use institution names as text; logos require a suitable source and usage rights.
Verify city-level reference coordinates; do not use private or precise residence coordinates.
No travel inventory is supplied. Fill data/photography.json from owner confirmation. Do not infer visited countries from the CV, Globe, residence, language or conference plans.
No photographs are supplied. Keep originals outside public/ and the tracked app repository. Publish only owner-approved, metadata-stripped derivatives.
Use reviewed country-level representative coordinates in the photography manifest. They locate albums, not camera GPS or exact travel routes.

publicDirectoryRule: Only approved website assets enter public/. The handoff, original TeX, evidence index and internal notes do not.
photographyPublicationRule: Draft, private, unconfirmed and test-fixture assets must not enter public/, generated routes, metadata, search indexes, client bundles or deployment archives.
